newsitem.title: USA: IMF staff and Sudan agree on economic program.
newsitem.headline: IMF staff and Sudan agree on economic program.

text.p: The staff of the International Monetary Fund and Sudan have agreed on an economic programme that, if implemented, would allow the country to retain its threatened membership in the IMF, the agency said on Monday.
The IMF executive board gave Sudan a last chance last month to deal with its arrears and come up with a reform programme or face being expelled, an almost unprecedented step.
The programme agreed with the IMF staff apparently meets the executive board's recommendations but still must be reviewed by the board for final approval.
"The staff of the IMF concluded an agreement on a programme with the Sudanese authorities in line with the decision taken by the executive board on Feb 13, 1997," the IMF said.
"This programme will be submitted for the examination and approval of the executive board in the coming weeks," it added.

The IMF said last month that Sudan needed to make scheduled repayments on its loan arrears to the IMF as well implement a programme of economic and financial reform that can be monitored monthly by the IMF staff.
The new programme does not provide any new money as Sudan is ineligible to use IMF financial resources. The IMF estimates that Sudan is $1.7 billion on arrears on its loans.
